questions.text: In one arm of communicating vessels there is a mercury column 16 cm high. What is the height of the kerosene column in the second arm (in meters)? The density of mercury is 13.6 g/cm³ and that of kerosene is 0.8 g/cm³.

Water is poured into one of the communicating vessels and kerosene into the other. If the height of the water column is 16 cm, find the height of the kerosene column (cm). The density of water is 1 g/cm³ and that of kerosene is 0.8 g/cm³.

Mercury is poured into one tube of communicating vessels. The second tube contains water. The height of the mercury column is 5 cm. If the mercury and water columns are in equilibrium, what is the height of the water column (cm)?

Water and kerosene are poured into a U-shaped communicating vessel. The water level is 30 cm below the top edge of the vessel. The other arm of the vessel is filled with kerosene. Find the height of the kerosene column (cm).

The second arm of a U-shaped communicating vessel has a radius 2 times larger than the first. If a liquid is poured into it, what is the ratio h1/h2 of the heights of the liquid columns in the first and second arms?

Two immiscible liquids are poured into a U-shaped (communicating) vessel. If the ratio of their heights measured from the interface is h1/h2 = 2, what is the ratio of the densities of these liquids ρ1/ρ2?

Communicating vessels initially contained water and mercury. The height of the water column is 68 cm. To what height (in cm) must kerosene be poured into the other arm of the vessel so that the mercury stands at the same height in both parts of the vessel?
Mercury, kerosene and liquid x are poured into communicating vessels as shown in the figure. Find the density of liquid x (kg/m³). (The kerosene column is 40 cm, the column of liquid x is 30 cm)
Mercury is poured into communicating vessels. Water of mass m = 204 g is poured into the arm of area S1 = 10 cm². By what height h (cm) does the mercury rise in the arm of area S2 = 5 cm²?
